subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Windshield Dangers
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Windshield Dangers.

hook.text: Early windshields were made of plain glass—the same kind used in house windows.

buildup.text: In a crash, the glass shattered into razor-sharp shards that sliced through passengers.

discovery.text: In 1903, a chemist dropped a flask coated in cellulose—it cracked but didn't shatter.

twist.text: This accident inspired laminated glass—two layers bonded with a plastic sheet between them.

climax.text: Ford adopted laminated windshields in 1927, and flying glass injuries dropped sharply.

punchline.text: A dropped flask saved millions of faces.

quiz.question: What inspired the invention of laminated windshield glass?

details.summary: Early car windshields shattered into deadly shards on impact. The development of laminated safety glass in the 1920s and later tempered glass for side windows dramatically reduced laceration injuries.
details.whyItMatters: Windshield glass was one of the most common causes of facial and eye injuries in early car crashes. Laminated glass holds together on impact, preventing occupants from being cut or ejected.
takeaways: Laminated glass has a plastic layer that holds fragments together
Tempered side windows break into small rounded pieces instead of shards
Modern windshields also support the roof structure in rollovers

faq.question: What is the difference between laminated and tempered glass?
faq.answer: Laminated glass has a plastic interlayer that keeps the pane intact when broken, used for windshields. Tempered glass shatters into small blunt pieces instead of sharp shards, used for side and rear windows.

faq.question: Does the windshield play a structural role in modern cars?
faq.answer: Yes. Modern windshields are bonded to the car frame and contribute to roof strength during rollovers. They also help direct the frontal airbag inflation correctly toward the occupant.
